questions.questionText: Using the data in Extract D (Figure 3), calculate the median number of storm overflow hours by water company in 2022.
Figure 2 shows the market for a good. S1 shows the supply if only private costs are considered and S2 shows the supply if social costs are taken into account. At the free market output, there is
options: a negative externality and overproduction of the good.
a negative externality and underproduction of the good.
a positive externality and overproduction of the good.
a positive externality and underproduction of the good.

questions.questionText: A government announces that, over a 10 year period, it plans to reduce the number of tradable pollution permits it issues each year. Which one of the following is the most likely response from firms in industries affected by the announcement?
options: Firms are likely to delay investment into more environmentally friendly production methods
Only the firms that generate the most pollution are likely to react at all
Over time, more firms will have an incentive to reduce their pollution
The firms with the lowest costs of reducing pollution will buy the most permits

questions.questionText: Table 1 shows the private benefit, private cost, social benefit and social cost of four different redevelopment projects. A local authority has a maximum of £15 million to spend on the redevelopment. Which one of the projects in Table 1 should the local authority choose to maximise social welfare, given the limited funding available?
options: Grants to new retailers
Marketing campaign
New bus station
Pedestrianisation

questions.questionText: Extract C (lines 3–4) states that ‘the mining, manufacturing and disposal process for batteries could soon become an environmental disaster.’ With the help of a diagram, explain why the production and sale of lithium-ion batteries might lead to market failure.

Extract B (lines 20–21) states that ‘all vehicle owners should be forced to pay the full costs of their driving. This would incentivise people to consider using public transport, cycling or walking.’ Evaluate policies that could be used to reduce the environmental impact of all types of car.

Hedges around fields encourage wildlife and bring widespread benefits but many farmers choose to have wire fences instead. Which one of the following best describes the resulting failure in the market for hedges?
options: The social optimum output is greater than the free market output because the private benefit is greater than the social benefit.
The social optimum output is greater than the free market output because the private benefit is less than the social benefit.
The social optimum output is less than the free market output because the private benefit is greater than the social benefit.
The social optimum output is less than the free market output because the private benefit is less than the social benefit.

questions.questionText: Figure 5 shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves for a product. The socially optimal level of output for this product is
options: 2 units
3 units
4 units
5 units

questions.questionText: A government plans to plant a new forest to provide a recreation facility and help combat climate change. Estimates of the costs and benefits are shown in Table 1. From the figures in Table 1, it can be concluded that the forest project will have
options: negative production externalities of £9 million.
positive consumption externalities of £16 million.
positive production externalities of £4 million.
total externalities of £25 million.

questions.questionText: Many goods are sold in plastic packaging that has harmful effects on the environment. In Figure 3, D1 and S1 are the free market demand for and supply of plastic packaged goods. S2 would be the supply if firms took account of the cost to the environment of plastic packaging. The government decides to implement a policy that would result in production moving from the free market level at Q1 to the social optimum at Q2. Which one of the following policies is most likely to achieve the government’s objective?
options: A subsidy at the rate P1 P3
A subsidy at the rate P2 P3
A tax at the rate P2 P1
A tax at the rate P2 P3

questions.questionText: Which one of the following is a reason why the extension of property rights is likely to reduce market failure?
options: Merit goods will no longer be underconsumed in a free market.
Producers will be more likely to have to pay compensation for pollution.
Public goods will no longer be subject to the free-rider problem.
The inequality in the distribution of income and wealth will be reduced.

questions.questionText: Figure 1 shows the marginal private benefit and marginal social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private cost and marginal social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in the market for a good. The diagram represents a good with
options: negative externalities in production and consumption.
negative externalities in production and positive externalities in consumption.
positive externalities in production and consumption.
positive externalities in production and negative externalities in consumption.

questions.questionText: The UK government has set a target to reduce net greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions to zero by 2050. To what extent, if at all, do the data suggest that to achieve its net-zero emissions target, the government should focus on reducing GHG emissions from the transport sector? You must use the data in Extract C to support your assessment.
Explain why, without government intervention, markets are likely to allocate too few resources to dealing with the problem of climate change.

Using the data in Extract A (Figure 1) calculate the percentage of all plastics produced in the period 1950–2015 which have either been sent to landfill or incinerated. Give your answer to one decimal place.
Explain how the data in Extract A (Figure 2) show that higher living standards lead to greater volumes of waste per capita being produced.

Extract C (lines 17–19) states: ‘Many environmental economists suggest that making firms pay for the costs of landfill associated with their products, or taxing raw material inputs, will be necessary to ensure a sustainable future for all.’ Using the extracts and your knowledge of economics, evaluate policies, if any, that governments in developed countries should pursue to reduce waste and encourage the recycling of waste products.

Figure 6 shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in the market for domestically produced solar panels. The initial market equilibrium is at E1. To correct the market failure, the government introduces a subsidy to domestic manufacturers of solar panels of £200 per unit produced. Which one of the following represents the total amount of subsidy payments made by the government in the first year of the scheme?
options: £20 million.
£25 million.
£75 million.
£100 million.

questions.questionText: The production of a good generates positive externalities. This means that at the free market equilibrium
options: the good will be under-produced.
the price of the good will be too low.
there will be excess demand for the good.
the supply of the good will be inelastic.

questions.questionText: In a free market, the consumption of a good leads to negative externalities. If left to the free market, how would price and output compare to the social optimum?
options: The price and output would be higher
The price and output would be lower
The price would be higher and the output lower
The price would be lower and the output higher

questions.questionText: A government plans to build a new road to bypass a small town. The table below shows the costs and benefits of two possible routes for the new road. The government intends to choose the route that has the higher ratio of social benefits to social costs. This ratio (correct to one decimal place) is
The existence of negative externalities in consumption results in a misallocation of resources. This is because at the free market level of output the
options: marginal private benefit is greater than the marginal private cost.
marginal private cost is greater than the marginal social cost.
marginal social benefit is less than the marginal social cost.
marginal social cost is less than the marginal private benefit.

questions.questionText: Smoking cigarettes generates negative consumption externalities. This means that
options: the private benefit from smoking includes the consumption externalities.
the social benefit from smoking is less than the private benefit.
the social benefit from smoking is negative.
the social optimum level of smoking is zero.

questions.questionText: Explain why the use of petrol and diesel cars may be a source of market failure.

Training provided by firms in a free market economy may be underprovided because some of the benefits from training may be captured by other firms when the workers change jobs. Which one of the following best describes this situation?
options: A negative production externality and a missing market
A negative production externality and partial market failure
A positive production externality and a missing market
A positive production externality and partial market failure

questions.questionText: Assess the view that regulation is a better policy for dealing with the problem of air pollution than the allocation of property rights or taxation.
To what extent, if at all, do the data suggest that the reliance on fossil fuels to produce energy is falling? You must use the data in Extract C to support your assessment.
Explain why, in a free market, sugary drinks may be overconsumed.

In the diagram below, D1 and S1 are, in the absence of government intervention, the market demand and supply curves for a vaccine. The demand curve D2 shows how much of the vaccine would have been demanded if the external benefits could have been captured by the market. The diagram illustrates that there is a misallocation of resources because in a free market
options: the price of the vaccine is too high.
there is excess demand equal to (Q3 – Q1).
there is under-consumption of the vaccine equal to (Q3 – Q1).
there is under-production of the vaccine equal to (Q2 – Q1).

questions.questionText: The supply and demand curves for a good in a free market are S1 and D1. If the good generates negative externalities in production but positive externalities in consumption, which intersection, A, B, C or D, could represent the socially optimal equilibrium?
options: Intersection A
Intersection B
Intersection C
Intersection D

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the marginal private and social benefit (MPB and MSB) curves and the marginal private and social cost (MPC and MSC) curves in a market where there are positive externalities in production. At the free market equilibrium, market failure occurs. Which one of the following is correct?
options: As a result of this market failure, consumer surplus is reduced by ZXY
As a result of this market failure, there is a deadweight loss to society of P3P1XZ
P1 minus P3 is the subsidy per unit that is required to correct the market failure and achieve the social optimum
The diagonal distance XY shows the amount by which marginal private cost exceeds marginal social cost at OQ2

questions.questionText: The diagram below shows the demand and supply curves for a good provided solely by a free market. Currently, output is at OQ1. However, there is a misallocation of resources resulting in market failure. The socially optimal level of production is OQ2. Which one of the following statements is correct? The diagram shows the market for
options: a merit good.
a public good.
a good with negative externalities in production.
a good with positive externalities in production.
